title: Clean up AtomicSaver after finalization failures
body:
## The change

`AtomicSaver.__exit__` flushes and syncs its part file before entering its cleanup handling. If either operation raises, the stream remains open and the part file is left behind even with the default `rm_part_on_exc=True`. A close failure also bypasses cleanup.

Always attempt to close the part file, and use one conditional cleanup path for finalization and rename failures as well as context-body exceptions. Flush/sync/close failures must not reach the rename step. Preserve the successful flush/sync/close/rename order, `rm_part_on_exc=False` for recovery, and the triggering exception when cleanup unlink fails.

This change does not address setup failures or change the existing precedence when both the context body and finalization raise. It attempts closing; if the OS itself fails to close a descriptor, this cannot guarantee actual closure. The existing Unix `overwrite=False` link-then-unlink rename behavior is unchanged, including the possibility that the target link already exists if the later unlink fails.

## The backstory

Related contribution: #535, which contains my contribution background. This issue was found during AI-assisted inspection of the documented atomic-save failure paths, not from a production incident. The reproduction injects `ENOSPC` at `os.fsync` while using a real part file; it is not a claim of testing an actually full disk.

## AI assistance

- Harness/tooling: OpenAI Codex desktop, with a separate read-only Codex code reviewer.
- Model(s): The exact serving model identifier is not exposed to this session.
- Original prompt(s), as close to verbatim as possible: “继续” (“Continue”). Prior task: “继续做开源” (“Continue contributing to open source”). Earlier workflow: “你可以自动进行 完成每次pr之后再停止” (“You may proceed automatically; stop after completing each PR”). The reviewer was asked to inspect the actual diff, failure cleanup, exception behavior, resource and filesystem effects, tests, and readiness without modifying the checkout.

## Verification

- Untouched Python 3.12 baseline: 678 tests and 12 subtests passed.
- New regression matrix before the fix: 10 expected failures, 11 passing controls. Failure cases showed unclosed streams or retained part files despite cleanup being enabled.
- Real-file tests cover flush/sync/close/rename errors, cleanup enabled/disabled, existing/absent targets, body exceptions, cleanup errors, and successful overwrite.
- Python 3.12: 29 fileutils tests passed; full suite and doctests: 699 tests and 12 subtests passed.
- Official Python 3.14 `tox -e py314`: distribution build, installation, all 699 tests and doctests passed, with five existing deprecation warnings in unrelated tests.
- Other interpreter versions and operating systems were not run locally.
- Independent read-only review passed, including a separate run of the 29 fileutils tests.
